study: Hanley et al. 2016, Let's Think Secondary Science (LTSS), EEF
eval_evidence: EEF-funded trial independently evaluated by the Institute for Effective Education, University of York; separate from the delivery org (Let's Think Forum) and program developers.
developer_evidence: LTSS CPD delivered by Let's Think Forum, the program developer/delivery body, via its own team of ~7 named tutors who built long-term relationships with each school's science department.
cascade_evidence: Let's Think Forum tutors delivered the CPD/training and tutor support to the science teachers directly; no train-the-trainer intermediary between the program and the participating teachers.
counterfactual_evidence: School-level RCT vs business-as-usual control; control schools continued their usual science lessons.
coaching_evidence: Support = 1 initial + 6 in-school training days and ~8 face-to-face tutor meetings, supporting an in-school learning group/peer coaching; the program did not incorporate a fixed schedule of tutor in-class observation cycles (observations led by the school's senior leader), so periodic rather than frequent in-class coaching.
student_dose_evidence: The 19 LTSS lessons over Years 7-8 are taught by the schools' own science teachers and replace standard science curriculum lessons (changed instruction), not an added tutoring/extra-minutes student dose.
maturity_evidence: Two-year program (Years 7-8); primary science outcome measured at end of Year 8, i.e. after a prior year of implementation.
